name: Sendspark
subcategory: screen recording, walkthroughs and product demos
tagline: Record lightweight personalized videos and generate recipient-specific landing pages

tiers.name: Solo
tiers.notes: Extra seats cost $49/month. The supplied snapshot said $15/month for Video Messaging; the current public self-serve lineup starts at $49/month.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: 3 seats; 20,000 stored videos; 250 dynamic-video minutes; 7,500 workflow tasks

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 10 seats; 100,000 stored videos; 1,000 dynamic-video minutes; 25,000 workflow tasks

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 25 seats; unlimited storage; 3,000 dynamic-video minutes; 75,000 workflow tasks

tiers.name: Agency
tiers.limits: Custom client workspaces, seats, minutes, tasks and support

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom deployment, security, integrations, seats and support

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 7-day trial without a card
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual subscriptions are non-refundable
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra seats cost $29–$49/month; dynamic-video overage costs $0.19–$0.39/minute and each extra 1,000 workflow tasks costs $2–$10 depending on plan.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Sendspark, record lightweight personalized videos and generate recipient-specific landing pages. The hard boundary is personalization at scale, crm workflows, hosting, and engagement tracking, plus capture polish, hosting, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Record lightweight personalized screen or camera videos with microphone audio, trim them, and generate recipient-specific landing pages.
whatYouLose: personalization at scale, CRM workflows, hosting, and engagement tracking
ongoingBurden: OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Sendspark because the recording itself is easy; the subscription removes upload, transcoding, sharing, organization, and support work. The recurring cost buys OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cap
priorArt.desc: Open-source screen recording and sharing product with modern desktop architecture.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Cap
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Records and hosts a video; recipient-specific sales pages are not part of the deal.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Video Messaging plan and a personal desktop recorder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Sendspark in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, ffmpeg, and SQLite; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: record lightweight personalized screen or camera videos with microphone audio, trim them, and generate recipient-specific landing pages.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Offer screen, window, or region capture plus optional microphone audio.
Show an always-visible recording timer and make stop available from the tray.
Create a non-destructive trim view with crop, zoom, cursor highlight, and text callouts.
Render locally through ffmpeg with sensible H.264 and WebM presets.
Generate a poster frame, transcript, and Markdown summary beside each video.
Provide copy-file-path and reveal-in-folder actions instead of mandatory cloud upload.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public cloud hosting.
Deliberately leave out viewer identity and engagement analytics.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workspaces and SSO.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
